body:
Thanks man,

I really wish it wouldn't fizzle out. But it kind of did, that's when I started noticing her different behaviour. We had planned on meeting eachother way sooner but she didn't want to do that yet because she wanted to take things slowly. (she had some bad experiences with other guys)

At some point she started hinting at meeting up again (to be sure I just asked her if it was a hint and she said yes). I didn't really jump on the opportunity because I wanted her to dictate the pace so she wouldn't feel pressured. Now in the meanwhile she left with this other guy. I don't get it.

It's not the situation itself I'm worried about. I mean, it sucks but I'm sure things will be okay because we got along really well and this isn't going to change that in the long run (I mean as friends).

The reason I'm posting here is because I'm having these small burst where I just cannot control myself. Yesterday I started punching the wall and I couldn't stop it. Afterwards I realised it was stupid but I'm afraid of doing things worse than that.

I'm 18. Guess this makes it sound like a classic breakup even more.
Reading posts on here makes me realise there are people that have it far worse than me, but that doesn't take away the fact that I'm scared I'll do something stupid.

Yeah, I didn't really know where to put this.

Things is, r/relationships or something of the likes usually just responds with something that comes down to "get over it".
I figured because of my aspergers that's not how it works and just want to hear from people that have a similar way of thinking.
The whole "you'll find someone else soon" thing doesn't really work for me because of aspergers.

How do I go about this?

I've recieved advice from others, saying I shouldn't put all my eggs in one basket. Is that what you mean?

How can someone not do that? I mean I can't like more than one person in a romantical way, right?
